requirements.notes_h3: Getting a New Zealand photo accepted

rows.label: Background
rows.value: Plain and light-coloured, with strong contrast and no shadows or objects behind your head

rows.label: Glasses
rows.value: Prescription glasses are allowed if they are not tinted or thick-framed, with a clear gap between eyes and frames and no glare. No sunglasses.

rows.label: Expression
rows.value: Neutral, mouth closed, eyes open, no smiling

rows.label: Head coverings
rows.value: Only for religious or medical reasons, with your face fully visible

notes: Selfies are rejected. Ask someone to take the photo from about 1.5 m away with the camera at your eye level.
Leave a clear gap above and around your head, and include your shoulders and upper chest.
Do not use filters, editing or AI tools to change how you look.
Scans of printed photos are not accepted.
For babies, lay them on a plain light-coloured sheet and take the photo from above.
NZ Passports provides an online photo checker. Run your downloaded JPG through it before you start your application.

how_to.title: How to make a New Zealand passport photo
how_to.step1_text: Have someone else take it (no selfies) against a plain light background, following the New Zealand rules below.
how_to.step2_text: Choose the photo. It is processed in your browser and never uploaded to a server.
how_to.step3_text: Centre your face, leave space above and around your head, and zoom so your head is the right size.
how_to.step4_text: Use "Download digital photo (JPG)". It is sized to the official upload spec shown on this page.

items.q: What size is a New Zealand passport photo?
items.a: NZ uses digital photos: a 3:4 colour JPG between 900–4,500 px wide and 1,200–6,000 px high, and between 250 KB and 5 MB. The digital download on this page is 1200 × 1600 px.

items.q: Can I take my NZ passport photo with my phone?
items.a: Yes, you can use your own device, but someone else must take it. Selfies are rejected because the short distance distorts your face.
Yes, prescription glasses that are not tinted or thick-framed, with no glare on the lenses and a clear gap between your eyes and the frames. Sunglasses are not allowed.
